claims.subject: fractional bell nozzle length L_f
claims.object: an equivalent 15 deg half-angle conical nozzle with the same throat area, radius below the throat and area expansion ratio
claims.statement: An equivalent 15 deg half-angle conical nozzle is the standard used to specify bell nozzles: an 80-percent bell nozzle's throat-to-exit length is 0.8 of that of a 15 deg half-angle conical nozzle having the same throat area, radius below the throat and area expansion ratio.
claims.quote: Commonly, an equivalent 15° half-angle conical nozzle is used as a standard to specify bell

claims.subject: bell nozzle length beyond about 80 percent
claims.statement: Bell nozzle lengths beyond approximately 80 percent do not significantly contribute to performance, especially when considering weight penalties (Figure 4-12 thrust efficiency versus fractional length).
qualifiers: read from Figure 4-12 trend; no numerical criterion stated
claims.quote: bell nozzle lengths beyond approximately 80 percent do not significantly contribute to performance

claims.subject: parabolic approximation bell nozzle contour
claims.object: a 1.5 R_t upstream throat arc, a 0.382 R_t downstream entrance arc from T to N, and a parabola from N to the exit E
claims.statement: In the parabolic approximation suggested by G.V.R. Rao, the contour immediately upstream of the throat is a circular arc of radius 1.5 R_t; the divergent contour is a circular entrance section of radius 0.382 R_t from the throat T to point N followed by a parabola from N to the exit E.
qualifiers: Figure 4-13; near-optimum-thrust design procedure, not an exact optimum
claims.quote: The nozzle contour immediately upstream of the throat

claims.subject: parabola initial and exit wall angles theta_n and theta_e
claims.object: Figure 4-14 as functions of expansion area ratio for L_f = 60-100 percent
claims.statement: The design inputs for a parabolic bell are throat diameter, nozzle length (or fractional length L_f based on a 15 deg cone), expansion area ratio, initial parabola wall angle theta_n and exit wall angle theta_e; theta_n and theta_e are shown in Figure 4-14 as functions of the expansion area ratio for L_f = 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 percent. On the original page theta_n rises and theta_e falls with expansion ratio for every L_f, over epsilon 5 to 50.
qualifiers: curve trends and extent are reviewer observations of the original figure (PDF p.100); digitized values with uncertainty are in the P1 comparison record, not source-stated numbers
claims.quote: shown in figure 4-14 as a function of the expansion area ratio

claims.subject: near-optimum thrust bell contour design
claims.object: parabolic approximation procedures suggested by G.V.R. Rao
claims.statement: One convenient way to design a near-optimum-thrust bell nozzle contour is the parabolic approximation procedure suggested by G.V.R. Rao.
claims.quote: parabolic approximation procedures as suggested by G.V.R. Rao
